source._multi_module_note: TRUE, and the module_dir on both binaries is ./server — the Go module lives in the server/ subtree of a monorepo, not at the repo root. That makes render_l009_kit vendor and build from inside ./server, which is what we need.

source._ee_stubs_note: server/enterprise keeps ONLY the empty ReadyStack placeholder.go that source_patches writes (cmd/mattermost blank-imports package enterprise). The vendored-tree strip and the sale-tar leak check (drive.py _ee_strip_sh / _ee_leak_check_sh) remove and refuse everything else under it.
source._ee_strip_note: Removes the Source Available tree from the ACQUIRED source before the CE audit and the tree hash, so the packaged source is genuinely CE-only. LICENSE.enterprise at the repo root is a SYMLINK whose content is the literal string 'server/enterprise/LICENSE'; ee_strip refuses to follow symlinks and deletes the link itself, which is the correct outcome. Note ee_strip acts on the acquire-stage tree only — the vendor stage clones fresh, so the BUILD is cleaned by source_patches below instead. Both are needed: one makes the archive CE, the other makes the binary CE.
source._build_env_note: BUILD_NUMBER IS A SECURITY-RELEVANT SETTING HERE, not cosmetic. server/Makefile defaults it to `dev` when empty, and then appends `sourceavailable` to BUILD_TAGS — which links the MSL metrics and elasticsearch code straight into the binary. An unset BUILD_NUMBER silently produces a non-CE build that looks fine. Pin it to the release tag. GOFLAGS=-buildvcs=false and -trimpath keep the build free of VCS stamps; upstream's own release.mk passes -buildvcs=false for the same reason.

vendor_build._note: FILESYSTEM-asset materialization, NOT a go:embed — the server serves the web client from a client/ directory next to the binary at runtime, so this output is carried into the runtime image by offline_stage_copies below rather than compiled in. npm (not pnpm/yarn): webapp/package-lock.json is the only committed lockfile and package.json declares engines node ^24 / npm ^11 with no packageManager field. `npm run build` is `node scripts/build.mjs`, which is exactly what upstream's `make dist` invokes. --include=dev is required because the build toolchain itself lives in devDependencies. The postinstall runs patch-package against the committed patches in webapp/patches/ (five at v12.0.0), which is offline-safe. LAST CMD MATTERS: the renderer's own cleanup is `rm -rf node_modules` at the repo ROOT only, so mattermost's webapp/node_modules — an npm-workspaces tree with a copy under each of seven workspaces — would ride into the exported vendored source. That is the L-A56 shape that deadlocked buildkit's local export on grafana's ~48k-file tree, and nothing downstream needs it: the offline stage builds from server/vendor and copies webapp/channels/dist, neither of which lives under node_modules. SUBSHELLS, not bare `cd`: the renderer joins these cmds with && into ONE RUN, so the working directory PERSISTS from one to the next. A second bare `cd webapp` would resolve against /src/webapp and fail on a directory that does not exist, and the paths in the two cmds after it would be wrong in the same way. Wrapping each cd in a subshell keeps every command anchored at /src.
